stories.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

Interestingly, that stays roughly stable whether you are resting or busy with a complex task. Image: Irina Romanova/Zoonar/picture alliance Advertisement You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes. Your brain has its own version of that. Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift? Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing. It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas. That's your brain's default mode network. But a new study suggests that for women, it can also lead to worse treatment from colleagues. Across 826 people in the United States and China , women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often. Men with high scores did not receive such treatment, and in one group, they were treated better.
